o: Support two operations on a circular red/blue tile array: count alternating groups of a given size s, and recolor a tile. Crucial reduction: an alternating group of size s exists starting wherever s consecutive tiles alternate, so the answer for size s is Σ over maximal alternating segments of length L ≥ s of (L − s + 1). Track the circle's 'bad' edges (adjacent equal-colored tiles); maximal alternating segments are exactly the arcs between consecutive bad edges, with tile-length = (edge-gap − 1) + 1. A recolor changes at most two edges, causing local arc splits/merges. Keep arc lengths in two Fenwick trees (count and sum) indexed by length so each size query is answered in O(log n) via Σ (L − s + 2) over L ≥ s − 1.
k: Groups of size s = Σ over maximal alternating segments L≥s of (L−s+1); maintain segment lengths in count/sum Fenwick trees.
A recolor flips at most 2 adjacency edges; each flip splits or merges one arc — O(log n) with an ordered set of bad edges.
Special case: if NO bad edges exist, the whole circle alternates and every size s ≤ n−1 has exactly n groups.

a.n: Approach 1: Bad-edge set + arc-length Fenwick trees
a.i: Store bad edges in an ordered set. Toggling an edge to bad splits its arc into two; toggling to good merges its two neighboring arcs. Each toggle updates the multiset of arc lengths (edge counts t; segment length t+1) in the Fenwicks. Query s sums t ≥ s−1 of (t − s + 2) = (sum − (s−2)·count).
s: Build the bad-edge set and initial arc multiset from colors.
Type-2 query: recolor, then for each of the two incident edges, if its good/bad status changed, split or merge arcs.
Type-1 query: if no bad edges return n; otherwise combine Fenwick prefix sums for lengths ≥ s−1.
a.t: O((n + q) log n) — each edge toggle does O(1) ordered-set/Fenwick operations, each query two Fenwick prefix sums
a.sp: O(n) for the Fenwick trees and the bad-edge set

w: This is the hardest of the three Alternating Groups problems; the whole battle is choosing the right decomposition (bad edges → arcs → segment lengths). Test carefully around the degenerate multiset states: zero, one, and two bad edges each need bespoke handling, and the fully-alternating circle (no bad edges) answers n for every size. Watch modular arithmetic on cyclic gaps (always normalize with ((x % n) + n) % n). Follow-ups: report groups of ALL sizes (prefix sums over the Fenwick), or tile insertions/deletions (balanced BST with subtree metadata).
